definitions.median_c5: close five sessions later ÷ next-session open − 1
definitions.ci_pct_dump: 95% bootstrap interval, 1000 resamples of whole dates
definitions.lift_dump: study dump rate ÷ dump rate of all rows where the condition could be evaluated

caveats: Conditional base rates, not a trading system: no borrow, fees or slippage.
Universe = names listed today (survivorship bias); delisted collapses are missing.
Filing-based studies only cover names with SEC filing history in the data.

baseline.title: All eligible name-days
baseline.condition: every labeled row (price ≥ $0.10, 20-day median $ volume ≥ $50k, ≥ 60 prior sessions)
baseline.plain: Across every eligible small/micro-cap session (1,704,908 cases across 3,634 stocks), the next session fell 5%+ from open to close 8.8% of the time (95% CI 8.4%–9.2%). Median open→close -0.1%; it closed below its open 50.9% of the time and squeezed 20%+ above the open 1.2% of the time. It also RAN UP 5%+ open→close 7.9% of the time (1.00× normal) — so this is mostly a bigger-move signal, not a clean downside one.

studies.title: All eligible name-days
studies.condition: every labeled row (price ≥ $0.10, 20-day median $ volume ≥ $50k, ≥ 60 prior sessions)

studies.title: Up 20%+ on the day
studies.plain: After a stock closed up 20% or more on the day (11,343 cases across 2,213 stocks), the next session fell 5%+ from open to close 37.3% of the time (95% CI 36.2%–38.5%) — 4.25× the 8.8% rate for comparable name-days. Median open→close -1.9%; it closed below its open 57.0% of the time and squeezed 20%+ above the open 15.6% of the time. It also RAN UP 5%+ open→close 25.2% of the time (3.18× normal) — the tilt is to the downside.
